## Purpose

This SOP describes the procedures for calibrating, operating, and
maintaining the Eureka Manta2 Sub2 Multiprobe for water quality
measurements including temperature, pH, depth, conductivity, and
dissolved oxygen (mg/L and % saturation) [@eureka_manta2; @apha2012].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Water quality measurements in lakes, streams,
  rivers, and other surface water bodies
- **Does not apply to:** Groundwater monitoring wells (requires
  different deployment procedures); laboratory bench-top water
  analysis
- **Location:** All EA Program field water sampling sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve protocol, ensure training compliance            |
| Field Lead        | Verify calibration before deployment, coordinate
                      logistics                                            |
| Trained Personnel | Calibrate, operate, and clean the probe per this SOP    |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |

### Required Training

Researchers using this SOP should be trained on
[SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd).


## Definitions

- **Amphibian 2:** The ruggedized handheld field computer (portable PC)
  manufactured by Eureka that controls the Manta2 probe, displays
  real-time readings, stores data snapshots, and connects to the probe
  via the underwater cable [@eureka_manta2].
- **Barometric pressure:** Atmospheric pressure at the measurement
  location, expressed in mm Hg; required as an input for dissolved
  oxygen calibration because oxygen solubility decreases with
  decreasing pressure (increasing altitude) [@apha2012].
- **Calibration:** The process of adjusting sensor readings to match
  known reference standards before field use; required before every
  field outing to ensure data accuracy [@eureka_manta2].
- **Conductivity (specific conductance, spCond):** A measure of a
  water sample's ability to conduct electrical current, expressed in
  µS/cm or mS/cm; proportional to the concentration of dissolved ions;
  temperature-corrected to 25 °C for comparability across sites and
  seasons [@apha2012].
- **Dissolved oxygen (DO):** The concentration of oxygen dissolved in
  water, expressed as mg/L or percent saturation (%sat); measured by
  the HDO sensor using luminescent optical technology; decreases with
  increasing temperature, salinity, and altitude [@apha2012].
- **HDO (Handheld Dissolved Oxygen):** The luminescent optical
  dissolved oxygen sensor on the Manta2; measures both %sat and mg/L;
  calibrated in water-saturated air or with an air-saturated water
  standard [@eureka_manta2].
- **PDOP (Position Dilution of Precision):** A dimensionless measure
  of GPS accuracy based on satellite geometry; lower values indicate
  better positional accuracy; values below 3 are acceptable for most
  field applications.
- **Reference electrode:** The electrochemical half-cell that provides
  a stable reference potential for pH measurement; requires periodic
  refilling with reference electrolyte to maintain accurate pH
  readings [@eureka_manta2].
- **Sensor Response Factor (SRF):** A calibration diagnostic value
  indicating how the sensor responded to the reference standard;
  acceptable ranges are sensor-specific and indicate whether
  calibration was successful [@eureka_manta2].
- **Snapshot:** A single instantaneous record of all sensor readings
  captured and stored by the Amphibian at a specific date, time, and
  GPS location.
- **Sonde (probe):** The cylindrical instrument body of the Manta2
  that houses all sensors (temperature, pH, conductivity, dissolved
  oxygen, and reference electrode) and is submerged during
  measurements [@eureka_manta2].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Biological/Chemical:** Water bodies may be contaminated; avoid
  ingestion and direct skin contact.
- **Physical:** Slippery surfaces near water; risk of submersion;
  electrical components near water.
- **Chemical:** pH standards (pH 4, 7, 10) and conductivity standard
  are mild irritants.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile or latex gloves
- [ ] Water shoes or wading boots (if entering the water)
- [ ] Safety glasses (during calibration with standards)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for
general field safety, transportation, and emergency response.


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Eureka Manta2 Sub2 Sonde              | Inspect sensors before each use          |
| Amphibian 2 field computer            | Ensure fully charged [@eureka_manta2]    |
| Underwater cable                      | Inspect for damage before use            |
| pH 4, 7, and 10 standard solutions   | For pH calibration; check expiration dates |
| Conductivity standard                 | Appropriate concentration for expected range |
| Deionized water                       | For rinsing sensors between calibration steps |
| Storage/calibration cup               | Filled with tap water for storage        |
| Field notebook                        | Per [SOP-F003](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd) |


## Procedure

### Startup

1. Connect the underwater cable to both the sonde and the Amphibian.
2. Power on the Amphibian.
3. Open the **Amp_2_2_6** app (or press **P1** shortcut).
4. Allow sensors to stabilize for 5--10 minutes before calibration.

### Calibration

Calibrate before every field outing [@eureka_manta2; @apha2012].
Record all calibration data (SRF values, standard concentrations,
date, operator) in the field notebook.

#### pH

1. Remove the storage cup. Rinse sensors with DI water.
2. Submerge the sonde in pH 7 standard. Select **Calibrate > pH**
   and follow the on-screen prompts.
3. Rinse with DI water. Submerge in pH 4 standard.
   Accept the second calibration point.
4. (Optional) Verify with pH 10 standard. Record the SRF
   (acceptable range: 95--105).

#### Conductivity

1. Rinse sensors with DI water.
2. Submerge in the appropriate conductivity standard.
3. Select **Calibrate > Conductivity**. Enter the standard value and
   accept [@eureka_manta2].
4. Record the SRF (acceptable range: 110--120).

#### Dissolved Oxygen (HDO)

1. Remove the sonde from the calibration cup. Allow the HDO sensor
   to equilibrate in water-saturated air for 2 minutes (sensor face
   moist but not submerged).
2. Enter the current barometric pressure in mm Hg.
3. Select **Calibrate > DO** and accept the 100% saturation
   calibration [@eureka_manta2].
4. Record the SRF (should equal 100%).

### Field Measurement

1. Lower the sonde to the desired depth. Allow 1--2 minutes for
   readings to stabilize before recording.
2. Press **Snapshot** on the Amphibian to save readings. Record the
   snapshot ID, location, and notes in the field notebook.
3. For depth profiles, lower the sonde in 0.5 or 1 m increments,
   pausing 30--60 s at each depth [@eureka_manta2].

### Disconnecting

1. Remove the probe from the water.
2. Disconnect the underwater cable from the probe.
3. Insert the blue storage plug.
4. Cover the cable end with the plastic protector.


## Post-Field Procedures

### Cleaning the Probe

1. Clean the probe with warm soapy water (liquid dish soap or mild
   household cleaner).
2. Clean sensor stems with a soft brush.
3. Rinse thoroughly with tap water.
4. Store sensors with tap water inside the cup.

### Downloading Data

1. Connect the Amphibian to your PC using a USB cable.
2. A green window will appear with four options; select
   **File Management**.
3. In the next window, navigate to the hard drive, then select
   **My Documents**.
4. Locate the Excel document with your data.
5. Copy the file to your project data folder.

### Charging

Return the Amphibian to its charging station after each field outing.


## Quality Control

- Calibrate all sensors before every field outing [@apha2012;
  @eureka_manta2].
- Verify SRF values are within acceptable ranges; do not proceed if
  any sensor fails calibration.
- Record a post-deployment calibration check on return to the lab;
  if any sensor has drifted beyond acceptable limits, flag the data.
- Compare spot readings against an independent DO meter or
  multiprobe where possible; readings should agree within ±0.3 mg/L
  for DO and ±0.1 units for pH [@apha2012].


## Troubleshooting

| Problem                        | Solution                                         |
|:-------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------|
| No power                       | Check the green LED on the Manta2; if off, the voltage is insufficient. Try another cable. |
| pH SRF out of range            | Recalibrate with fresh standards. If still out of range, refill the reference electrolyte and contact the PI. |
| Conductivity SRF outside 110--120 | Recalibrate. If still out of range, contact the PI. |
| HDO %sat SRF ≠ 100             | Redo the calibration with freshly aerated water. |
| GPS not acquiring satellites   | Ensure the top cap (antenna) is uncovered; move to an open area. |

## Training Record

Before using this instrument independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) training
3. Observe a trained operator perform calibration and field deployment
4. Perform a supervised calibration of all sensors
5. Perform a supervised field deployment with data collection
6. Be signed off by the field lead or PI
